Population: Rainfed smallholder farming households in savings groups
Community_Context: Rainfed smallholder farmers organised in VSLAs
Problem: Rainfall variability destroys harvests and repayment capacity, pushing families deeper into poverty; climate shocks go uninsured.
Product_Concept: Parametric drought-index insurance bundled into VSLA crop loans, with the premium financed into the loan principal so cover is automatic rather than opt-in.
Design: Cluster RCT: villages randomised to bundled cover versus loan-only, premium financed into principal
Primary_Outcome: Consumption smoothing conditional on index-measured drought exposure; 90-day-past-due incidence
Toolbox_Fit: RT-1 schema captures agro-climate and geospatial tags; RT-3 monitor watches rainfall-index triggers; impact module measures consumption smoothing through shocks. ⚠️ EVIDENCE WARNING 2026-08-22: this design - premium financed into principal so cover is compulsory rather than opt-in - is precisely what was tested and failed in LIT-024 (Malawi, take-up 13 points lower) and LIT-025 (India, 16 point rise in drop-out). Do not carry it forward as written without answering why it would go differently here. See OQ-17.
Candidate_Partners: VSL Associates / CARE VSLA network; J-PAL regional office; a local index-insurance underwriter
Candidate_Funders: J-PAL King Climate Action Initiative; 3ie; IDRC

Population: Off-grid rural households reached through savings groups
Community_Context: Off-grid rural households reached through VSLAs
Problem: Energy poverty and biomass-cooking emissions; households cannot finance solar home systems or clean cookstoves.
Product_Concept: PAYGO-style clean-energy asset loan originated through the VSLA under a group guarantee, with repayment data standardised for later pooling.
Design: Staggered rollout across group clusters with matched difference-in-differences; RCT where a distributor will randomise
Primary_Outcome: Repayment completion rate on the asset loan; clean-energy adoption and biomass displaced
Toolbox_Fit: Underwriting engine uses group repayment signals; securitization modelling on the clean-energy receivables pool.
Candidate_Partners: PAYGO solar distributors; VSLA networks; energy-access sector bodies
Candidate_Funders: Shell Foundation; IKEA Foundation; FSD Africa

Population: Smallholder cooperative members on water-constrained plots
Community_Context: Smallholder cooperatives on water- and land-constrained plots
Problem: Climate stress on land and water; smallholders lack capital for climate-smart dual-use solar-plus-agriculture.
Product_Concept: Cooperative project-finance vehicle blending PPA revenue and crop revenue, with a DFI first-loss layer to attract senior capital.
Design: Single-vehicle demonstration with pre-post and matched comparison; not randomisable at realistic scale
Primary_Outcome: PPA and crop revenue realisation against model; cost of senior capital achieved
Toolbox_Fit: Waterfall modelling and PPA cash-flow verification carried over from PL-2; schema extended to cooperative membership.
Candidate_Partners: Agricultural cooperatives; a DFI blended-finance desk; a utility offtaker

Population: Grain-farming households aggregated through savings groups
Community_Context: Grain-farming households aggregated through savings groups
Problem: Climate-driven price volatility and post-harvest loss force distress sales at the bottom of the market, entrenching poverty.
Product_Concept: Warehouse-receipt-backed lending via VSLA aggregation, with cover against storage loss, letting farmers borrow against stored grain and sell when prices recover.
Design: Phased rollout across warehouses with difference-in-differences on sale timing and price realised
Primary_Outcome: Price realised per unit sold relative to harvest-time spot; distress-sale incidence
Toolbox_Fit: Standardised warehouse receipts become poolable receivables; monitoring tracks storage conditions and price triggers.
Candidate_Partners: Warehouse operators; commodity exchanges; VSLA networks

Population: Pastoralist households whose livestock is their main asset
Community_Context: Pastoralist communities whose livestock is their primary store of wealth
Problem: Drought kills livestock, the main asset of the poor, driving recurrent poverty traps.
Product_Concept: Index-based livestock insurance bundled with savings-group credit, paying out on satellite-measured forage scarcity before animals die (building on the index-based livestock insurance precedent).
Design: Cluster RCT on bundled index-based livestock cover, building on an established index protocol
Primary_Outcome: Livestock mortality and distress sales through a drought season; herd retention
Toolbox_Fit: Index triggers, monitoring and impact-evaluation modules; schema captures herd and geospatial data.
Candidate_Partners: Existing index-based livestock insurance programmes; pastoralist associations
Candidate_Funders: J-PAL King Climate Action Initiative; IDRC

Population: Urban and peri-urban low-income households in climate-exposed settlements
Community_Context: Urban and peri-urban poor in climate-exposed informal settlements
Problem: Recurrent climate shocks - flooding, but also drought/heat and storms - destroy the productive assets of low-income households, resetting them into poverty.
Product_Concept: Multi-peril parametric climate cover (flood, drought/heat, storm) paired with a resilience-retrofit microloan, financed through community groups. Access to the cover is randomised, so the impact design stays clean even though the product spans several triggers.
Design: Cluster RCT: settlements randomised to multi-peril cover plus retrofit loan versus loan-only
Primary_Outcome: Productive-asset retention through a peril event; speed of recovery
Toolbox_Fit: Schema plus multi-peril parametric triggers; RT-3 monitor doubles as an early-warning signal. Shares a trigger to payout to loss-avoided measurement design with EXP-01.
Candidate_Partners: Urban community-based organisations; municipal partners; a parametric underwriter
Candidate_Funders: J-PAL King Climate Action Initiative; Rockefeller Foundation; Green Climate Fund

Geography: MENA remittance corridors (Gulf to North / East Africa)
Population: Remittance-receiving households in climate-vulnerable home regions
Community_Context: Remittance-dependent households in climate-vulnerable home regions
Problem: Households reliant on migrant remittances hold no formal savings or climate cover, so a shock abroad or at home cascades into poverty.
Product_Concept: Remittance-linked savings-and-microinsurance product anchored to a home-side community group, converting part of each transfer into resilience cover.
Design: Encouragement design on the sending side with matched comparison on the receiving side
Primary_Outcome: Formal savings balance and cover in force at time of shock; consumption smoothing
Toolbox_Fit: Data schema extended to remittance inflows; underwriting on transfer regularity.
Candidate_Partners: Remittance service providers; home-side community groups

Population: Women-led micro-enterprises in the clean-energy value chain
Community_Context: Women-led micro-enterprises in the clean-energy value chain
Problem: Energy-access SMEs (solar distributors, clean-cooking retailers) lack working capital, throttling both clean-energy diffusion and poverty-reducing income.
Product_Concept: Revolving receivables-backed working-capital facility for a pool of clean-energy micro-enterprises.
Design: Phased facility rollout with matched difference-in-differences on enterprise outcomes
Primary_Outcome: Enterprise turnover and stockholding; facility loss rate
Toolbox_Fit: Underwriting engine and securitization modelling on trade receivables.
Candidate_Partners: Clean-energy distributor networks; women's enterprise associations

Population: Smallholder coffee growers in producer cooperatives
Community_Context: Smallholder coffee growers organised in producer cooperatives with existing certification and traceability systems
Problem: Coffee income collapses on the joint hit of price volatility and climate stress (leaf rust, drought, heat), and pre-harvest credit is repaid at exactly the wrong point in the price cycle.
Product_Concept: Pre-harvest credit through the cooperative bundled with a climate trigger and a price floor, so that repayment obligations flex with realised revenue rather than compounding the shock.
Design: Cluster RCT randomising cooperatives, or stepped wedge where a lender will not withhold
Primary_Outcome: Household coffee income through a shock season; loan completion rate at cooperative level
Toolbox_Fit: RT-1 schema maps onto existing certification records; RT-3 monitors both climate triggers and price; RT-5 pools cooperative receivables that a lender already finances.
Candidate_Partners: Producer cooperative federations; agricultural value-chain lenders; certification bodies

Population: Smallholder coffee growers exposed to leaf rust and heat stress
Community_Context: Coffee-growing households in cooperatives in rust-prone and heat-stressed altitudes
Problem: Coffee leaf rust and heat stress destroy multi-year plantings, and the loss is a slow-onset event that conventional indemnity cover prices badly and index cover has rarely been built for.
Product_Concept: A climate index calibrated to rust and heat-stress conditions rather than rainfall alone, bundled with replanting credit so a payout funds recovery rather than consumption.
Design: Cluster RCT on cover access, with index performance validated against observed loss
Primary_Outcome: Plantation survival and replanting rate after a rust or heat event; basis-risk rate of the index
Toolbox_Fit: Index design and trigger monitoring; schema captures altitude, varietal and plot-level agro-climate tags.
Candidate_Partners: Coffee research institutes; producer cooperative federations; parametric underwriters
Candidate_Funders: J-PAL King Climate Action Initiative; IDRC; Green Climate Fund

Population: Certified coffee cooperatives and their existing lenders
Community_Context: Coffee cooperatives already operating under certification and traceability regimes that capture transaction-level data
Problem: Certification and traceability systems already collect much of what an origination schema would demand, but the data was built for provenance claims rather than for credit, and nobody has tested whether it can carry underwriting.
Product_Concept: Repurpose existing traceability and certification records as an origination data tape, and test whether receivables against certified sales can be pooled without new field data capture.
Design: Design-science build against real certification data, validated by out-of-sample default prediction
Primary_Outcome: Share of RT-1 required fields satisfiable from existing records; predictive lift over a no-data baseline
Toolbox_Fit: Directly tests RT-1 against a live data source; if it holds, the marginal cost of securitisation-ready capture in this value chain is near zero.
Candidate_Partners: Certification bodies; agricultural value-chain lenders; cooperative federations

Geography: Adaptable - any savings-group or SHG setting
Population: Savings-group members and the groups themselves as borrowers
Community_Context: Savings groups receiving external loan capital, in a network large enough to randomise the lending level
Problem: Securitisation removes the community as the individual-level creditor, which is the layer the evidence says does the actual work. Whether the local information advantage survives depends on where the external creditor attaches.
Product_Concept: Randomise whether external capital is lent to the group as a single borrower that on-lends to members, or directly to members with the group as guarantor. Contract economics held constant.
Design: Cluster RCT on lending level, with mechanism measures (screening decisions, monitoring contact, sanction events)
Primary_Outcome: Member-level default rate; measured local information use in screening decisions
Toolbox_Fit: This is the empirical test of OQ-13 and it determines which structure RT-1 and RT-5 must be built for.
Candidate_Partners: Savings-group network operators; an MFI willing to vary its lending structure; an academic field team

Geography: Adaptable - any savings-group setting with external funding available
Population: Savings-group members borrowing from mixed funding sources
Community_Context: Savings groups where some loan capital is the members' own accumulated savings and some is externally supplied
Problem: The mechanism evidence points at repeated interaction and members' own money at stake. Securitisation substitutes outside money for community money, and no study has randomised that substitution.
Product_Concept: Randomise, within treated groups, whether the loan fund is the group's own savings or external wholesale capital, holding terms and lending capacity constant.
Design: Second-layer randomisation within a cluster RCT (research-framework section 3)
Primary_Outcome: Repayment rate and arrears trajectory by funding source; informal risk-sharing measures
Toolbox_Fit: Tests the assumption every downstream tool rests on. A null result clears the pooling thesis; a negative result redirects the venture to the group-level structure.
Candidate_Partners: Savings-group network operators; an academic field team; a wholesale lender

Geography: Adaptable - savings-group networks at formation stage
Population: Newly formed savings groups
Community_Context: Savings groups at formation, where promoting NGOs already set constitution rules as a matter of course
Problem: Group rules on buffers and emergency funds are set by convention rather than evidence, and they plausibly determine whether a shock becomes a default.
Product_Concept: Randomise the constitution: capital buffer size and whether the group runs a separate emergency fund alongside the loan fund.
Design: Cluster RCT on rule variation at group formation, low marginal cost because rules are being set anyway
Primary_Outcome: Default incidence through the cycle; share of shocks absorbed without missed repayment
Toolbox_Fit: Cheapest way to test whether formal underwriting substitutes for or complements group self-insurance.
Candidate_Partners: Savings-group promoting NGOs; VSLA network trainers

Population: Savings-group members
Community_Context: Established savings groups where repayment information is currently shared informally or not at all
Problem: The information channel and the sanction channel can trade against each other. Which one disclosure strengthens is testable and has never been tested directly in this setting.
Product_Concept: Randomise whether individual repayment performance is disclosed to the full group, to officers only, or not at all.
Design: Cluster RCT on disclosure regime with measured social-cost outcomes alongside repayment
Primary_Outcome: Repayment rate; measured social sanction and group cohesion
Toolbox_Fit: Separates the information and sanction channels that Ghatak and Guinnane describe, using a lever a lender could actually pull.
Candidate_Partners: Savings-group promoting NGOs; an academic field team

Population: Smallholder borrowers on seasonal income cycles
Community_Context: Savings groups lending against seasonal agricultural income
Problem: Rigid repayment schedules are a poor fit for seasonal income and may generate defaults that reflect timing rather than capacity.
Product_Concept: Randomise repayment structure: rigid schedule, grace period, or income-flexible schedule tied to harvest timing.
Design: Cluster RCT on repayment structure
Primary_Outcome: Default rate and arrears volatility; household investment during the cycle
Toolbox_Fit: Cash-flow shape is exactly what a securitisation prices, so this speaks to both estimands at once.
Candidate_Partners: MFI and savings-group network partners

Population: Borrowing households offered climate cover
Community_Context: Savings-group members offered cover alongside credit
Problem: Automatic cover financed into principal produces near-universal take-up, but it is then impossible to tell whether measured effects come from protection or from who ends up covered.
Product_Concept: Offer the same actuarial product three ways: financed into principal, opt-in at the same price, and opt-in with a subsidy that equalises take-up.
Design: Three-arm cluster RCT separating the protection effect from the take-up effect
Primary_Outcome: Resilience outcome conditional on shock, decomposed into take-up and protection channels
Toolbox_Fit: Answers the design question every bundling result depends on, and is a cheap add-on arm to any of the parametric pilots. PROMOTED IN IMPORTANCE 2026-08-22: the LC-04 read makes this the central experiment rather than an add-on arm. LIT-024 and LIT-025 show compulsory priced-in cover suppresses demand; LIT-026 shows demand is strong when cover is offered separately. Separating the take-up effect from the protection effect is therefore the live question in this literature, and this is the design that does it. See OQ-17.
Candidate_Partners: Any originator running a bundled pilot; an academic field team

Population: Smallholder households facing covariate climate risk
Community_Context: Savings groups in areas with an indexable climate peril
Problem: Insurance and contingent credit are alternative answers to the same problem, and the sector assumes insurance is better without having raced them directly.
Product_Concept: A drought-triggered contingent credit line versus a parametric insurance payout of equivalent expected value.
Design: Three-arm cluster RCT: contingent credit, parametric cover, control
Primary_Outcome: Consumption smoothing and asset retention conditional on trigger; cost per unit of protection delivered
Toolbox_Fit: Contingent credit is far cheaper to structure than insurance and needs no underwriter, so a null difference would change the product roadmap.
Candidate_Partners: MFI partners; parametric underwriters; an academic field team
Candidate_Funders: J-PAL King Climate Action Initiative; 3ie; IDRC

Population: Savings-group member households
Community_Context: Savings groups where health shocks are a documented cause of default
Problem: Health shocks are consistently among the largest causes of both household distress and loan default, and they are idiosyncratic - exactly the risk community structures are supposed to be good at.
Product_Concept: Health microinsurance or a health-contingent repayment holiday bundled into group credit.
Design: Cluster RCT on bundled health cover versus credit alone
Primary_Outcome: Default incidence attributable to health events; out-of-pocket health expenditure and asset sales
Toolbox_Fit: Idiosyncratic risk diversifies inside a pool far better than covariate climate risk, so this may be the stronger securitisation case even where it is the weaker climate story.
Candidate_Partners: MFI and savings-group networks; health microinsurance providers

Geography: Adaptable - mixed and single-gender group settings
Population: Women-only and mixed savings groups
Community_Context: Savings-group networks containing both women-only and mixed groups
Problem: Savings groups are predominantly women's institutions, and a design that ignores intra-household bargaining will mis-attribute its own effects.
Product_Concept: Bundled cover offered across groups of differing composition, with intra-household allocation measured.
Design: Cluster RCT stratified by group composition, with pre-specified heterogeneity analysis
Primary_Outcome: Resilience outcome by group composition; intra-household allocation of the payout
Toolbox_Fit: Heterogeneity here is a publishable result in its own right and a required robustness check on every other bundling estimate.
Candidate_Partners: Savings-group networks; an academic field team

Population: Savings groups currently keeping paper ledgers
Community_Context: Savings-group networks operating on paper record-keeping
Problem: Digitising the group ledger is a precondition for poolable data, but the act of recording may itself change behaviour - which would make the measurement instrument an intervention.
Product_Concept: Digital group ledger with standardised fields, rolled out against continued paper record-keeping.
Design: Cluster RCT on ledger digitisation, measuring behaviour as well as data quality
Primary_Outcome: Repayment rate change attributable to digitisation; completeness and error rate of captured records
Toolbox_Fit: Directly tests whether RT-1 capture is behaviourally neutral, which every downstream estimate quietly assumes.
Candidate_Partners: Savings-group network operators; digital financial services providers

Geography: Adaptable - any originator running two protocols
Population: Loan officers and originating groups
Community_Context: An originator willing to run two origination protocols side by side
Problem: The claim that designing for securitisation at origination beats retrofitting it has never been tested, and neither has its cost.
Product_Concept: Securitisation-ready origination protocol (full RT-1 field set) versus the originator's standard protocol, on randomly assigned branches or officers.
Design: Randomised protocol assignment with activity-based costing of both arms
Primary_Outcome: Marginal operational cost per household of the fuller protocol; marginal gain in default predictability
Toolbox_Fit: The direct test of RQ-06 and one of the two falsification tests that can run before any product pilot.
Candidate_Partners: An MFI or savings-group network with branch-level operations

Population: Impact investors, structurers and credit analysts
Community_Context: Professional investors and analysts recruited through fund networks and industry bodies
Problem: The sector assumes investors will not price community-originated assets because the data is poor, but nobody has measured what disclosure actually changes a price.
Product_Concept: Present a synthetic community-originated data tape to investors with randomly varied disclosure - track record length, field granularity, verification status - and elicit indicative pricing.
Design: Framed field experiment with randomised information sets and incentivised elicitation
Primary_Outcome: Indicative spread quoted, and willingness to engage at all, by disclosure condition
Toolbox_Fit: Turns RT-5 output into a research instrument. Needs no field site, no IRB burden beyond standard human-subjects review, and no partner NGO.
Candidate_Partners: Impact-investor networks; microfinance investment vehicle managers; industry associations
Candidate_Funders: Academic small-grant schemes; institutional research funds

Population: Rating analysts, structurers and DFI credit committees
Community_Context: Professionals who decide whether an asset class is rateable
Problem: Whether a rating agency will engage with community-level receivables before a track record exists is the open residual on OQ-2, and it is currently unanswered because nobody has asked systematically.
Product_Concept: Structured elicitation and scenario review with raters and structurers on eligibility criteria, minimum track record, and what would have to be true to rate this asset class.
Design: Delphi-style structured elicitation with pre-registered scenario set
Primary_Outcome: Stated minimum conditions for engagement; convergence across respondents
Toolbox_Fit: Converts the biggest unknown in the securitisation thesis from speculation into documented expert opinion, and doubles as relationship-building.
Candidate_Partners: Rating agencies; structuring advisers; DFI blended-finance desks

Population: Existing loan portfolios of savings-group networks and MFIs
Community_Context: Historical management-information-system data from one or more originators across regions
Problem: The pooling thesis rests on defaults being idiosyncratic rather than covariate. If they are covariate, diversification buys far less than assumed and the structure does not work.
Product_Concept: No product. Estimate default correlation across groups, regions, time and agro-climatic zones from existing portfolio data.
Design: Multi-level correlation estimation on historical administrative panels
Primary_Outcome: Estimated cross-group and cross-region default correlation; covariate share of total variance
Toolbox_Fit: Feeds RT-5 the one parameter it currently assumes. A falsification test that can run before any pilot exists.
Candidate_Partners: MFI and savings-group networks willing to share historical data; sector data repositories

Population: Existing savings-group and microfinance loan books
Community_Context: A historical loan book with observed defaults and recoveries
Problem: There is no published loss curve for community-originated lending in a form a structured-finance analyst would recognise, which is why the asset class cannot be priced.
Product_Concept: No product. Fit survival and hazard models to time-to-default and time-to-claim, and estimate loss given default from observed recoveries.
Design: Survival analysis with horizon sensitivity on historical panels
Primary_Outcome: Fitted default hazard and loss-given-default estimates with stated confidence bounds
Toolbox_Fit: Produces the loss curve RT-5 currently synthesises, and is publishable independently of any pilot.
Candidate_Partners: MFI and savings-group networks; sector data repositories

Population: Simulated pools calibrated to observed parameters
Community_Context: Model portfolios built from whatever empirical parameters are available
Problem: The enhancement level required to reach investment grade is asserted from blended-finance averages rather than derived from this asset class, and the sensitivity of that number is unknown.
Product_Concept: No product. Systematic sensitivity analysis of first-loss thickness, originator diversification and reserve design against modelled loss distributions.
Design: Monte Carlo waterfall simulation with full parameter sweep
Primary_Outcome: Required first-loss thickness for investment-grade loss characteristics, and its sensitivity to each input
Toolbox_Fit: RT-5 already exists; this is the study that turns it from an internal tool into a paper. Weak alone, strong once EXP-25 or EXP-26 supplies real parameters.
Candidate_Partners: None required

Population: Participants in published savings-group and microcredit trials
Community_Context: Replication archives of completed randomised evaluations
Problem: A large body of savings-group RCT data exists and has been analysed exclusively for treatment effects. Nobody has re-read it for the cash-flow properties a financial engineer would want.
Product_Concept: No product. Re-analyse published trial data for repayment timing, arrears distribution and variance rather than mean treatment effects.
Design: Individual participant data re-analysis with hierarchical pooling across trials
Primary_Outcome: Pooled distributional properties of repayment behaviour across contexts; between-study heterogeneity
Toolbox_Fit: Cheap, fast, publishable, and it directly tests how far risk parameters travel between sites.
Candidate_Partners: Trial authors and replication archives; academic collaborators

Population: Migrant workers in employer-linked savings and lending arrangements
Community_Context: Migrant-worker communities operating informal savings arrangements within a regulated employment framework
Problem: Migrant workers save and lend informally with no formal cover, and a shock at home or in employment cascades into loss of both income and status.
Product_Concept: Savings product with income-protection cover anchored to an existing worker network, used primarily as a controlled setting to develop the protocol and data pipeline.
Design: Small-n pilot with matched comparison; the value is protocol development, not identification
Primary_Outcome: Protocol and instrument performance; take-up and cover-in-force; data completeness
Toolbox_Fit: Logistically accessible testbed for the RT-1 pipeline, the survey instruments and the consent protocol before deploying somewhere harder.
Candidate_Partners: Worker associations; Israeli community development organisations; a local academic research centre
Candidate_Funders: Local foundations and academic funds - note Israel is ineligible for most development-research grant streams

Population: Insured smallholder households
Community_Context: Smallholder farmers under an index insurance product
Problem: Basis risk is the standard explanation for weak index-insurance demand, but whether reducing it is worth its cost has not been established.
Product_Concept: The same cover verified two ways: a satellite-derived area index versus picture-based or field-verified loss assessment.
Design: Cluster RCT on verification method, with both measures collected for every household
Primary_Outcome: Measured basis-risk rate by method; welfare effect per unit of verification cost
Toolbox_Fit: Feeds the index-design side of RT-3 and answers whether cheap-and-imperfect is the efficient design.
Candidate_Partners: Parametric underwriters; agricultural research institutes; an academic field team
Candidate_Funders: J-PAL King Climate Action Initiative; IDRC; Green Climate Fund
